about: Building codes, one entry each, read by `building_code` and `stair_check` (codes.rs). A project names one and starts with its rules, which it may change (a state's or a city's own rules); nothing built is ever refused for breaking one, only reported. A country's code is added as a new entry, never as code. Unless an entry says it was `checked`, its numbers were typed from memory of the documents named, not from their text, and each code tells occupancies apart where an entry holds one row (the general one); check a number against a copy before relying on it. Where a code gives no number, the entry holds a forgiving one that asks nothing in practice, and `note` says which. Millimetres. `stairs`: `riser` and `going` are what a new stair starts with; `riser_min`..`riser_max` and `going_min`..`going_max` their ranges; `step_min`..`step_max` the range of 2 risers + 1 going; `width_min` the least clear width; `headroom` the least height over the walk line; a landing is due when a flight would rise more than `flight_rise_max` or hold more than `flight_risers_max` risers, whichever comes first; `landing_rule` says how long a landing must be: `width` the stair's width, `landing_length` being enough; `fixed` `landing_length`; `step` a going and one step (2 risers + 1 going), and `landing_length` at least. `winders` whether winding treads are allowed; `walk_line` where their going is measured: `centre` along the middle, `narrow_side` at `walk_line_offset` from the narrow side; `winder_going_min` the least going there and `winder_narrow_min` the least at the narrow end. `nosing_max` the most a tread overhangs; `open_risers` whether risers may be open; `uniformity` the most two risers or goings of a flight may differ; `handrail_min`..`handrail_max` a handrail's height over the nosings; `guard_min` a guard's least height. `nosing_min` the least a nosing stands out. `sources` gives, rule by rule, the document, its edition and its item a number is from, or says it is a forgiving number no document gives; `checked` says who checked the entry against the documents' text.

codes.name: No building code
codes.note: No code's numbers: wide ranges round common practice, so a stair is reported only when it is far from any stair one would build.

codes.name: ABNT NBR 9050 (accessible route)
codes.checked: Checked against the text of ABNT NBR 9050:2020 by a contributor (pull request #386).
codes.note: For a stair on an accessible route. An emergency exit is held to NBR 9077 instead (the next entry), and in most states to the fire brigade's own instruction, which rules over it (São Paulo's IT 11, Santa Catarina's IN 09). Curved and mixed flights are allowed when the tread and riser on the walk line keep to 6.8.2. Headroom and the most risers in a flight are not in the standard: forgiving numbers. Risers within a flight are constant; 0.5 mm is the tolerance used for that.

sources.going: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.2, a tread in its range
sources.headroom: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (2.10 m is the standard's height for doors and passages)
sources.flight_rise_max: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.7, a landing every 3.20 m of rise
sources.flight_risers_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (3.20 m ÷ 160 mm)

sources.walk_line_offset: NBR 9050:2020 6.8.6, 0.55 m from the inner edge

codes.name: ABNT NBR 9077 (emergency exit)
references: ABNT NBR 9077:2001 (saídas de emergência em edifícios), 4.4 dimensionamento, 4.7 escadas, 4.8 guarda-corpos
codes.checked: Checked against the text of ABNT NBR 9077:2001 by a contributor (pull request #386).
codes.note: For an emergency exit stair. In most states the fire brigade's own instruction rules over this standard (São Paulo's IT 11, Santa Catarina's IN 09): change the rules to its numbers. The width here is two units of passage (1.10 m); the standard sizes it by the population. Balanced winders are allowed (4.7.9.1) except on smoke-proof stairs and in occupancy groups F and H (4.7.9.2). Successive flights may differ by 5 mm in riser at most (4.7.3.1); within a flight the risers are equal, 0.5 mm the tolerance. An internal stair's guard may drop to 0.92 m (4.8.1.2) and an external one more than 12 m up needs 1.30 m (4.8.1.3). Headroom and the most risers in a flight are not in the standard: forgiving numbers; it asks 3 risers to a flight at least.

sources.going: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.3.1, a tread in its range
sources.width_min: NBR 9077:2001 4.4.2, two units of passage (sized by the population)
sources.headroom: Not in the standard: a forgiving number
sources.flight_risers_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (the standard asks 3 at least)
sources.landing_rule: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.3.3, by the formula for straight runs
sources.landing_length: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.3.3, and no shorter than the width
sources.winders: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.9.1, balanced winders (not on smoke-proof stairs or in groups F and H, 4.7.9.2)
sources.walk_line_offset: NBR 9077:2001 3.32, 0.55 m from the inner edge
sources.winder_narrow_min: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.3.1 and 4.7.9.1, 0.15 m at the narrow end
sources.uniformity: NBR 9077:2001 4.7.3.1, equal within a flight (0.5 mm tolerance)
sources.guard_min: NBR 9077:2001 4.8.1.2, 1.05 m (0.92 m inside, 1.30 m outside over 12 m)

codes.name: International Building Code
codes.note: The general row; inside a dwelling the IBC and the IRC allow a riser of 7 3/4 in and a going of 10 in. The IBC has no step rule and counts no risers in a flight: `step_min`, `step_max`, `going_max` and `flight_risers_max` are forgiving numbers. Winders are allowed inside dwellings only. Inches, written in millimetres.

sources.flight_risers_max: Not in the code: a forgiving number
sources.landing_rule: IBC 2021 1011.6, as deep as the stair is wide
sources.landing_length: IBC 2021 1011.6, 48 in where the stair runs straight
sources.walk_line: IBC 2021 1011.5.3, 12 in from the narrow side
sources.winder_going_min: IBC 2021 1011.5.3, 11 in at the walk line

codes.name: DIN 18065
codes.note: The row for buildings in general; a house of up to two dwellings may have a width of 800, a riser of 200 and a going from 230. The European Union has no stair code of its own: each country has one, and this is Germany's. DIN counts risers, 18 in a flight at most, so `flight_rise_max` is a forgiving number, and so is `nosing_max`.

codes.name: Building Standards Law of Japan
references: Building Standards Law Enforcement Order, articles 23 to 25 (stairs, landings, handrails)
codes.note: The row for buildings not otherwise listed; schools, theatres and large shops have stricter rows, a dwelling a looser one. A winder's going is measured 300 from its narrow end. The order gives no riser minimum, going maximum, step rule, headroom, riser count or uniformity: those are forgiving numbers.
